title: Generalizing a Pair of Diophantine Equations
summary: For coprime integers $a$ and $b$, it is known that exactly one of the two Diophantine equations $$ ax+by\ =\ \frac{(a-1)(b-1)}{2} \qquad\text{and}\qquad 1+ax+by\ =\ \frac{(a-1)(b-1)}{2} $$ admits a nonnegative integer solution, and that this solution is unique. We first generalize this result by replacing the right-hand side with an arbitrary integer $m$ and its complement $ab-a-b-m$. This framework enables us to study the existence and uniqueness of nonnegative integer solutions to $$ ax+by\ =\ \frac{(a-1)(b-1)}{k} \qquad\text{and}\qquad 1+ax+by\ =\ \frac{(a-1)(b-1)}{k}, $$ where $k$ is a…
